senses.def: Excluding the person(s) being addressed. (This is the exclusive we.)
ex: We are here to arrest you.

senses.def: The institution which the speaker/writer is acting for. (This is the editorial we, used by writers and others when speaking with the authority of their publication or organisation.)
ex: We will in due course state our reasons for publishing the name of the accused.
As the government, we have a duty to ensure public safety.

senses.def: Any other entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, nation, region, language, etc.
ex: I went to watch our school football match against Puddletown High. We lost 2-0.
In English, we do not inflect adjectives for gender.
We still have much to learn about quantum mechanics.

senses.def: The sovereign alone in his or her capacity as monarch. (This is the royal we. The reflexive case of this sense of we is ourself.)
ex: We are Queen of all these Isles.
Good evening everyone. How are we all tonight?

senses.def: An individual being addressed; used especially to a person in the speaker's care, or to whom advice or instruction is being given. (Sometimes called the nurse's we or the doctor's we.)
ex: Hello Mrs Miggins. How are we feeling this morning?
You've been spending all your money boozing when you have a wife and family to support. I think we need to get our priorities straight.

senses.def: Used to refer to a third person, especially someone in the speaker's care.
ex: "I've just been to see Mrs Miggins." — "And how is she?" — "I'm afraid we aren't too good today."

senses.def: Used to imply connection between the speaker's experiences or activities and a group of listeners. (Compare the plural of modesty.)
ex: Hey guys, in this video I'll show you how I make my upside-down sponge cake. First we take 200 g of butter and we whisk in 200 g of sugar. Next, we ...

senses.def: Used in explanatory or procedural writing, such as mathematical explanations, to imply inclusion of the reader in the undertaking.
ex: To solve the equation, we first collect all the terms in x on one side.

senses.def: Used when talking to oneself to refer to oneself.
ex: Now then ... let me see ... I hope I'm doing this right ... if we just connect these two wires together ...

senses.def: The side which is keeping score.
Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as belonging to or constituting the stated category of people.
ex: We Canadians like to think of ourselves as different.
We the undersigned wish to express our disapproval.
